notes: Works and handles a root pointing at a symlink plus over-long seeks. However, squashfs lookup is a convoluted exact-then-suffix retry with Remote() comparisons, and zip Open gains symlink-only EOF special cases.

Correct for both backends, including clamped zip seeks and root-at-link, but squashfs New and NewObject rely on remote-equality retry logic that is more roundabout than naming entries the way List does.
Code is identical to the reference. It adds sensible zip and squashfs tests (including a hostile-archive CopyDir check) and a short docs section.
Code matches the reference for both zip and squashfs, with a short docs section and solid tests for skip vs --links, a regular .rclonelink member, and an end-to-end hostile-archive escape.

Close to the reference for both zip and squashfs. Minor oddities: a directory entry carrying the symlink mode is treated as a file, the log names only --links, and one squashfs range read in the test is never asserted.

Close to the reference, with squashfs lookup naming entries as List does; it slightly changes how trailing-slash symlink entries are treated, and one squashfs test reads a range result without asserting it.

Zip matches the reference. The squashfs exact/suffix lookup refactor correctly hides unsuffixed link names and supports a root at a symlink. Tests are thorough (copy, escape, root-at-link, regular .rclonelink).

Zip change matches the reference and the squashfs exact-then-suffix lookup correctly keeps List and NewObject consistent, though NewObject can now return a typed-nil *Object inside a non-nil interface; tests cover copy, escape and root-at-link.

Functionally fine and resolves name collisions in favour of regular members. That collision check linearly scans the directory on every zip/squashfs entry add, making listing quadratic for large directories, and it adds a binary fixture.

Works and also resolves regular-vs-link name collisions, but the collision check scans every existing entry for every object in both readZip and squashfs List, making large archives O(n²), and the squashfs New/NewObject logic is convoluted.

The shared OpenLink helper and bounded target read are clean. But the zip suffix is added after root matching, so a root naming link.txt.rclonelink is not found, and squashfs root lookup has the same mismatch, making root naming inconsistent with listing.

Adds the link suffix only after root matching, so a root pointing at the listed 'x.rclonelink' name is not found while the unsuffixed name becomes a single object; it also decompresses every zip symlink eagerly at list time and adds a shared helper the task did not need.

It drops symlinks whose targets are absolute or point above the root, and drops links whose suffixed name collides with another entry; this goes against the spec that symlinks are listed, fails a hidden test, and leaves out very common absolute links. It also reads the flag from the VFS options instead of fs.GetConfig(ctx).Links and adds a new base package plus complex root-trimming logic.

Reads the VFS links option instead of the global -l/--links config and silently drops legitimate absolute or parent-relative symlinks via a new safety filter, which contradicts the spec; it also adds heavy root/conflict machinery and fails a hidden test.
